Those who channel Death mana are divided into two factions, who utterly despise each other. The larger faction are practitioners of Undeath magic who pervert the sphere to create abominations despised by Arawn. The minority who honor Arawn and try to use Death magic ethically are often persecuted and falsely condemned for heinous crimes committed by Necromancers, as most denizens of Erebus do not know or care to learn the difference between the two groups.

The precept of Death is about surrender and resignation, intended to balance the perseverance of the precept of Life. It is the rest for which a soul longs once it is weary of the world. It allows the old to get out of the way and to make room for the new. During the first few generations of man, death was rare and almost always welcome. The widespread fear of death today is a sign of the world's corruption.
Most Death magic in Erebus is actually Undeath magic, a terrible deviation from what the Death sphere is supposed to represent. The
are created by magic that binds the souls of the departed to the world of the living. This is extremely unhealthy both for them and the world around them, leading to much corruption.

Arawn has never been a very active god. He tried to stay out of the Godswar, although the mortal warlord Barbatos tried to take the war to him and invade his vault. As punishment he barred Barbatos from ever entering the Netherworld, so he would be forever dying but never find rest. He treated Maoliosa and the Silkies much the same. When this caused a proliferation of necromancers creating ever worse abominations, he withdrew himself even further so as to limit their access to death mana rather than taking them out of the world of the living.

The Unblemished teach that Arawn gifted the power of Life to Sucellus out of recognition of their god's superior virtue, but this is a lie. When embodying both Life and Death, Arawn had to die and rise again each year on Samhain. Sucellus used the opportunity of Arawn's death to steal the Font of Life, allowing him to raise himself as the new God of Life while leaving Arawn languishing as an almost powerless ghost of his former self. Such decisions angered many of his servants, who have abandoned him to follow Basium or Laroth. A few of his loyal angels care enough to help the archangel Gyra defend the realm and carry out the duties that should be his.

Arawn was always very dour, but generally benevolent. He prefers to shelter the souls of the departed, not manipulate them into serving his purposes. The Compact demands that Arawn judge spirits of the dead to determine which god has the strongest claim, and then and pass them on their vaults to be made into angels or demons. He has been very lax in this duty. He prefers to leave the spirits to wander in the vast dreamland of his Netherworld, where the subconscious of each mortal soul fashions the sort of afterlife it believes itself to deserve. This is usually more fair than any reward or punishment any god could devise, but there are a few strong souls whose lucid dreams grant them undeserved power. The archmage Laroth is building an army of such souls in the hope of usurping the precept and becoming a god.

Dimensional promotions cause a summoner to keep a portion of its summons experience points when they die.
This resource causes unhappiness and a diplomatic penalty with many leaders. It causes a diplomatic bonus with those evil leaders who wish to destroy the world.

Dimensional is the sphere of relational identity. It was created to establish bonds between individuals, but since Ceridwen's fall has been more focused on breaking these bonds. Ceridwen leads us to value others only based on what they are to us, rather than appreciating them for who they really are. This leads to very unhealthy relationships, obsessions, and emotional pain. A master who defined himself by his position relative his servant will abuse the servant. He will fear loosing his position and never be able to turn their relationship into a friendship. A servant who obsesses over his own lowly estate will envy and despise his master rather than improving his own lot or enjoying life. A husband who is paranoid that his wife will be unfaithful will drive her away through his jealousy.

The sphere of Earth does not pertain merely to its physical manifestations, the elements of rocks and dirt that make up the ground beneath us. Deep down, it is about valuing the virtues of honest labor and the benefits it allows us to reap. Those who exemplify this sphere are often considered too stuffy and conservative, but they prefer to think of themselves as well grounded. Physical manifestations of this magic are however strengthened by contact with massive blocks of stone and weakened when standing on dirt or cut blocks. Practitioners may lose all affinity for this dominion if they aren't in contact with the earth at all. Being in a tree, on a horse, or simply held up in the air by someone else will negate their ability. But when in contact the practitioner can call on all aspects of the world to either imbue themselves with these aspects or transform the earth and stone around them.

The sphere of Enchantment is the opposite of the Dimensional sphere. It has to do with valuing the individual for his own individual virtues, regardless of his position in society. This leads to happier relationships. It is the sphere of improvement. The sphere leads us to make our natural strengths stronger. This dominion never works overtly. Instead the aspects of objects are enhanced by it. Without other dominions, only existing aspects can be heightened, a wall can be made stronger, a sword sharper. But with ties with fire a sword can be given a burning blade, or with darkness a charm can be made to hide the wearer. These spells take complex rituals and days, weeks, months or years to cast depending on their complexity. Practitioners of this dominion are typically collectors of obscure and varied objects. They can sense the affinity an object has for a dominion and they are quick to gather ones with a strong affinity because it makes enchanting them in that dominion much easier. A practitioner skilled in this dominion and death is likely to have a morbid collection of items strong with death affinity nearby, murderer's knives, gravedigger's shovel, pieces of gravestones, hangman's noose, etc. They occasionally find affinity for an item that they don't expect (a key with a strong affinity for mind magic) and can spend a lot of time trying to research the history of the object to find out why.

Entropy was originally the sphere of Hope, but Agares hoped for the impossible and turned his sphere into Despair. He is now the leader of the evil gods, and seeks to ruin Erebus out of spite just as he ruined his won world of Nyx. This sphere focuses on the unmaking, ruin and destruction of objects, people, and society, not by overwhelming power, but by finding and intensifying the targets' inherent flaws. This power often works unintentionally. Flowers wither, clothes unravel, and food spoils just because a practitioner is around. Users are often unable to maintain relationships; they see the flaws in others to closely. They become solitary and depressed, often suicidal.

Fire is the element of passion, of acting out uncontrollably based on emotion and of rapid change. It was once a holy precept, a great righteous indignation that empowered men to purge evils from the world. At the end of the Age of Magic, the Goddess Bhall was corrupted. She fell from her heaven, and tore it asunder as she plummeted into the deepest hell. (Her archangel
refused to be corrupted and continues to embody her element as it once was, but she was locked away in the
. ) Now that she has reawakened, her fury has turned against the good. Fire is wild and hungry, easy to use but difficult to control.

The power to channel and control fire also applies to rapid change and mutation. There is often great power in these transformations, but they are temporary and often leave the target weaker or even destroyed by the experience. Practitioners that internalize their power often consume an external source to feed it (fire, hatred or physical matter that they reduce to ash) so that they aren't destroyed by it. Practitioners of this dominion are very passionate lovers and artist, or are very violent. They are often very driven individuals, obsessively pursuing their goals and looking to launch rebellions among the disenfranchised.
This resource causes a diplomatic bonus with many leaders, and a penalty with those who wish to destroy the world.

Force is the power of the immutable. The power of authority and judgement. Magic is performed as "Decrees", the Decree of Eternal Vigilance compels someone to protect the target with their life. The Decree of Silence keeps someone from ever speaking about a subject and the Decree of Sanctity keeps the target from entering a specific location. Decrees can apply to people or inanimate objects. Powerful practitioners can have decrees that impact the entire world. A "wall of force" isn't a physical construct, it is a decree that nothing can pass the area that is applied to the entire world. Many practitioners of this dominion are mute. They tend to be open minded and thoughtful, but once they make a decision, they are slow to move off of it.

Force is the sphere of Balance, Compromise, Consensus, Agreements, and Contracts. Force does not have an opposing sphere; its opposite is an excess in any direction. It is prone to "The Grey Fallacy," assuming that the proper course of action is to compromise between opposing positions even if one is clearly better than the other or even if the compromise is worse than both. When both alternatives are bad, it can have trouble seeing which one is worse. The moderation of this sphere is however better than any extreme in most circumstances.

Dagda, the God of Force, does not support unilaterally imposing one's will on another; he is however just as harsh as Junil when it comes to making someone keep his word or go along with what an overwhelming majority has decided. Dagda is the god most responsible for creating the plane of Erebus and its inhabitants. When The One ordered his angels to create worlds in the image of Heaven, they all created world far too tainted by their own preferences. Dagda convinced them to work together, each angel pairing up with his opposite in order to create worlds of balance and contrast. Once everyone saw that these worlds were superior to any they could create alone, he convinced them all to collaborate and make Erebus together. This world so pleased The One that he declared their work finished and took back the power of ex nihilo creation. The gods still had enough power left for their greatest creation: Mankind, a race of beings who possessed the divine spark of the gods within forms that perfectly balance all 21 elements, allowing a level of free will which the angels could not imagine.
The Godswar was sparked by the disagreement over what to do with
, and escalated to the point that the survival of Humanity and even Erebus itself was threatened.

, the archangel of Dagda, convinced his god to bring the neutral gods together and force the war to end. The Compact was his idea, but he could not accept the agreement. One he learned of The One, he had no respect for these petty gods whose idea of peace was continuing to wage their war through human pawns.

Ice is the force of stasis, of unchanging. It can also be a force for calm or slow recovery (like a coma). A little power can cause things to slow, and strong practitioners can cause natural processes to stop entirely. Practitioners become dogmatic, resistant to new ideas or reform. They love tradition and take comfort in rituals and habits. They tend to be conservative in all things.

Ice is not merely conservative, but reactionary. It considers the past better then either the present or the future. It is nostalgia, a longing for the way we think things used to be (even if our memory is inaccurate). The One intended for this to complement the constant, gradual, progressive change of the sphere of Nature. When Mulcarn fell, it did not change much. He remained far less evil than the other evil gods. Since Sucellus stayed out of the war, he became the enemy of the rapid change of Bhall. During the Age of Magic, the forces of Bhall became so powerful that Mulcarn was nearly powerless. When he saw the advancements of that age, and how all gods but himself had come to be widely worshiped, he wished that mankind would return to how they lived during the Godswar. When Agares finally corrupted Bhall, he saw a chance. Unopposed, he was able to break The Compact and conquer Erebus itself. He defeated Sucellus when he came to stop him, but eventually fell to the Godslayer. In the Age of Rebirth, the Precept of Winter itself longs to return to the time when a god controlled it. The Illians long to return to their golden age.
intends to fulfill these desires and become the new

This dominion is the power of justice and equity. It punishes inequity, corruption and randomness. Law frequently gives power equal to any just challenge, but no more. Practitioners tend to be obsessive compulsive in some aspect of their lives. They are reliable administrators but may be inflexible. Practitioners are the most powerful when standing against corruption.

Law is the sphere of justice, but mostly the sphere of order. It values submission to authority and adherence to rules and regulations over freedom. Junil is the eldest of the Twenty One gods, and sees himself as their leader. He is extremely stern and unyielding. He cannot tolerate anyone breaking commandments. Despite this, he himself (like all the gods) broke The One's commandment when he agreed to make Man immortal, and again when he decided to use the power of the Gems of Creation against Agares rather than allowing his power to run out and become like a human himself. He also swore not to get involved in creation, before establishing a powerful religion for the purpose of countering the influence of demonic forces. The appearance of the Luonnotar has left him terrified that The One has returned and is not pleased with him.

Minor practitioners can influence fertility and help speed healing. More powerful can perform miraculous healing or extend life. Practitioners can also sense back through generations of a subject, sensing who assessors are, and bringing out their assets in their descendant. Practitioners are often conceived without sex. Those conceived like this often have high affinity. Practitioners are often drawn to those that are suffering, though they are often sought by powerful men as a balm against disease and old age.
Life is the sphere of Perseverance and Self-Sacrifice. It is about risking all you have in order to achieve a greater goal. It is also about healing, about coming back after what seemed like defeat.

The first God of Life was Nemed, but he sacrificed his precept in order to become the progenitor of the human race. He gave his godhood to Arawn, who embodied both Life and Death for three whole ages but always favored his original sphere. Arawn created twin archangels, one for each precept. Arawn stayed out of the Godswar (except to tend the souls of its many mortal casualties), but The Archangel of Life was always eager to fight. Basium frequently begged to be made God of Life himself so he could wage his war better, but Arawn always refused. Basium would not give up the fight even when ordered to do so by all the gods, but instead chose to fall and become a mortal as far as The Compact is concerned. At the end of the Age of Ice, Sucellus stole the Font of Life, leaving Arawn languishing as an almost powerless ghost so that he could resurrect himself as the new God of Life. Most men and gods view Sucellus as a champion of Good, but Basium hates him as much as the demons.

Meta Magic is the sphere of Knowledge and Memory It is focused on having an accurate understanding of the past. The One intended for this sphere to compliment Mind, which once dealt with predicting the future and now deals with trying to control it. Oghma's vault is home to a great library where secrets are kept that even the gods do not know. Mammon has invaded his vault trying to uncover these secrets. He conquered significant portions of it and convinced many of his angels to defect, before the God of Knowledge responded by filling the world with a mist that erases memories. Most of Mammon's troops have completely forgotten who they are and why they are there.

This dominion focuses on the nature of magic itself. It is most commonly used to detect and identify magic. Though at moderate levels it can be used to break and disrupt spells and at the highest levels it can be used to transform magic, or the way it works. A master in this dominion can create an area where magic doesn't work, move an enchantment from one object to another, or trap a magical creature in an object. This dominion has to be accessed through symbols, runes and ritual. Practitioners spend long hours studying to understand these complex interactions much as a chemist studies chemistry. This makes for bookish, arcane sorts. Unusually there are varied types of this dominion that seem to have little connection to each other. One may understand magical interactions through precise mathematical drawings, another through colorful mandala, other through carvings on elaborate 3 dimensional objects. These all have the same result, but students of each have little to learn from each other. It appears that any way it is envisioned it is only an interpretation for the true nature of magic, and practitioners can only hope to learn by continuing to learn more about their particular interpretation. Learning another is like starting over.

Mind was the sphere of Foresight, meant to compliment the backwards looking sphere of Knowledge. Mammon foresaw a time when he could foresee no more, and feared his own death. He rebelled against The One in order to prevent this fate, which ended up making it come true. His desire to predict was replace by a desire to control.

The power of memory and thought. Practitioners can read minds and protect their thoughts from the same. The more powerful can manipulate the memories of their targets or dominate them entirely. There are a wide range of effects that can be caused by this dominion, from becoming "invisible" by causing on target to fail to notice you, to implanting thoughts (you should go out on patrol), or mistaking the senses (that stick is a snake). The effects typically require concentration to maintain the effect. This dominion is largely ineffective against those whose minds are significantly different than the practitioners (so a human would be unable to affect animals or angels).

Exposure to others minds often causes befuddlement or confusion in the practitioner. They are often unable to simply cause the change they want and will expose themselves to other thoughts or memories of their targets. Practitioners who use the power to frequently may begin to dream as if they were their target, or have odd memories from the lives of those they have influenced. Many go insane. Others suffer dementia where their memories become lost in sea of others.

Nature is the sphere of growth, maturation, and gradual, progressive change. It was created to balance the stasis of the sphere of Ice. Sucellus tried to stay out of the Godswar, entering it only near the end to rescue his archangel Cernunnos from Agares' hell. He then sided with Dagda and the other neutral gods to try to being the conflict to and end and force the signing of The Compact. Once Bhall fell and Mulcarn broke the compact, Sucellus was chosen to enter Erebus and stop stop him. He failed. His body was broken into seven pieces, and his spirit departed into the Netherworld like that of a mortal. He tended the soul of the dead for an age, until Mulcarn was destroyed by the Godslayer and his body was brought back together. He took over the sphere of Life and was resurrected, but did not think himself still able to embody Nature properly. As such, he entrusted Nature to Cernunnos.

The power of the forest and the remote corners of the world can sense the life of a region and commune with plants and animals. Affinity is strongly based on the practitioners environment, being nearly powerless in urban areas and powerful in the deep forest. Practitioners often have a specific type of plant or animal that they bond with.

Shadow was created to be he sphere of Trust. It allowed more intimate relationships by allowing individuals to confide in each other without fearing that their secrets would be shared with everyone else. Since the fall of Esus, it has come to represent Deception, the abuse and betrayal of trust.

This is the power of deception, hiding and illusion. Unlike other dominions that give the power to detect their power, that is not granted through shadow. A practitioner can create illusions of size and complexity depending on his affinity. Many practitioners lose their affinity during the day. Nearly all practitioners have increased ability to see in darkness. Many with an affinity for this dominion see things that aren't real. Occasionally it is as strong as full hallucinations, but more commonly they are simply people moving in the shadows, something standing at the edge of the bed, or something glimpsed out of the corner of the eye that isn't really there.
Elohim
may also grant units Spirit Affinity, if you have an Infernal Pact Lethe.

Spirit is the sphere of Compassion, Empathy, Altruism, and Mercy. It embodies the Fruits of the Spirit. It is called the sphere of Wisdom, but the world often sees the wisdom of this sphere as foolishness. Most of the gods see Sirona like a nice little sister whose opinions do not really matter. Sirona was a close friend of Agares before his fall. The fall hurt her greatly, but she refuses to believe that evil the most evil of the gods is beyond redemption. Sirona forgives the wicked before they repent, in the hope that this forgiveness will lead them to repentance. She is the most clearly Good of the gods, but her sphere can be used for evil as well. Laroth was a master at using Spirit magic to read and manipulate the emotions of others. He tricked them into performing acts of self sacrificing and mutilating themselves to serve his purposes instead of their own good.

This is the power of emotion, of hope and fear, of compassion and anger. It is the power that reminds us that our bodies are a thin veil for the soul that lies within us. Bodies that will break down when we experience true loss, and unable to stand under overwhelming grief.

Twins are more likely to be gifted in this dominion. Blindness increases a practitioners affinity so it is more common in this dominion. Some practitioners blind themselves on purpose for this reason. Practitioners often unintentionally affect the emotions of those around them, because of that, they make good performers. Some practitioners have more powerful impact over those they love, some have more impact over those they hate.

Sun is the sphere of Truth, Light, Revelation, Insight, Openness, and Honesty. It is benevolent, but often harsh. It shows its love through constructive criticism. Lugus is eager to forgive, but careful not to forgive those who have not yet truly repented. He does not forget past wrongs, but keeps a watchful eye out for any signs of sliding back into sin. The sphere of Light is the source of the human conscience. In psychopaths like Vampires who lack a conscience, the light of Lugus is experienced like physical pain and psychological panic.

This is the power of revelation and spiritual truth. At modest levels it can destroy illusions and force the truth out of someone, and at the most powerful it can tear away everything false from a target, both physically and emotionally.

It can strike those that refuse to see the truth blind, turn strong but insecure men into burnt reflections of their spiritual selves, and shock a rioting mob into seeing exactly what they have become.

Telling lies weakens the power of a practitioner over this dominion. To the point that they can lose it entirely. Those that are completely open for years can reach amazing levels of power, but that is rare to find. Many casters are powerless at night, or when they are not in direct sunlight.

Water is primarily about how one addresses emotions. Fire is impulsive, compelling one to act out irrationally as soon as an emotion is felt. Water is about calmly and rationally contemplating the emotions in order to better understand their cause before doing anything about them. It is an essential element of the wisdom of old age and the true intimacy and deep commitment of companionate love. It easily dismisses petty offenses, but may ruminate (particularly on issues related to one's loved ones) enough to lead to depression and withdrawal when it is not clear what can be done to make a situation better. Danalin, the God of Water, was among the least involved in the Godswar. He never went abroad to fight, but stayed at home with his beloved Aifons to protect them. He grieved when the Compact required him to depart from them, and grieved far more when a great calamity annihilated the race completely. That drove him into a depression so deep that we fell asleep and refuses to wake up. Hastur, the Archangel of Mammon and Lord of Nightmares, now whispers terror into his ears. The god is an effective dreamer, whose nightmares have given rise to the Undertow. PARAGRAPH]The force of the ocean is also the power of dreams, sleep and madness. Their power is strengthened with contact with water, but most are able to draw off of the moisture in the air and in their own bodies to cast. PARAGRAPH]In the Age of Rebirth, most practitioners struggle with horrific nightmares. The intensity increases with their affinity with this dominion. Ironically many gifted with affinity in this dominion are afraid of water, either that fear or an early trauma with water seems to have deepened their connection.
